evals.prompt: I have a membrane protein with a ligand (resname LIG) loaded in VMD with a 500-frame DCD trajectory. Plot the ligand's z-position over time to see if it permeates through the pore. Make it publication quality.
evals.expected_output: A Tcl extraction loop computing ligand COM z-coordinate per frame, followed by a matplotlib script producing a publication-quality line plot with proper axis labels (Time in ns, z-position in angstroms), pore region shading, and both PNG/SVG output.

evals.prompt: Generate a contact map showing which pore-lining residues interact with the ligand across the trajectory. I want a heatmap figure I can put in a paper.
evals.expected_output: A Tcl script computing per-frame residue contacts within a distance cutoff, writing a data file, then a matplotlib heatmap (imshow) with residue IDs on y-axis, frames/time on x-axis, colorblind-safe colormap, and publication formatting.

evals.prompt: Make a composite 3-panel figure for my paper: top panel shows ligand-pore distance over time, middle panel shows number of hydrogen bonds per frame, bottom panel shows pore radius profile at the first and last frames. Save as SVG.
evals.expected_output: Multiple Tcl extraction steps (distance, hbonds, pore radius at two frames), then a single matplotlib script producing a 3-panel figure with shared x-axis where applicable, panel labels (A, B, C), proper units, and SVG output.
